Balrijin (Y85)

Region (English scoring-table grouping): Haless.

One-line positioning: Lead the Goldscale Kobolds in search of the missing golden dragon Balris, and grow the clan council from a frontier theocracy into a trade republic that includes multiple peoples.

Story: Very high｜Mission-tree length: Long (55 direct Y85 missions)｜Mission-tree update: use the current local scripts supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0｜Uniqueness: Very high｜Tedium: Medium-high (dragon search, diplomacy, and mission prerequisites)｜Early pressure: High｜Expansion ability: Above average, with alliances more important early

A Goldscale Minor

Balrijin already exists in 1444; it is not a formable country that appears only after finding the dragon. The base game gives Y85 two starting provinces, Goldscale Kobold culture, the Accretive Path faith, a Sage Council-style theocratic government, and the ruler Fax Akar, who appears in 1397. It has historically friendly relations with neighbors such as Lanjinhui, but its starting position is still fragile: the Halessi map, where humans, Oni, ogres, and the Command intersect, does not make room for safety merely because the Goldscales possess an ancient legend.【Local history script】

Balrijin's national self-description revolves around the golden dragon Balris. For the Goldscales, Balris taught their ancestors knowledge and order, but departed over the course of the long centuries; the sages must preserve his teachings while answering a more practical question: if the dragon does not return, how can a minor survive? This is not a story in which the deity has already been found at game start. The first half of the mission tree has different clans provide martial, divinatory, intelligence, and diplomatic resources while the country gradually follows clues; reunion with Balris is a future the player must pursue.【Local narrative text】【Local scripts】

The offline English Wiki places this legend in a longer history: around 500 AA, Balris brought the Goldscale tribes, which had previously lived underground, into organized society and taught them craftsmanship, learning, and governance; after he left, the clans maintained their community through faith in “He Who Shall Return.” In the early 15th century, Balrijin also resisted Jiangdu's expansion, supported the Blue Scarf peasant uprising, and recognized the new republic after the 1434 ceasefire. These are fixed-Wiki worldbuilding claims; the current base game's two-province start and mission effects still require script authority.【Offline Wiki】

Governing Beyond the Dragon Search

The Goldscale martial clans come into conflict, so the Sage Council moves training facilities away from the capital and tries to turn youthful competition into a manageable institution. Meanwhile, the diviners and spies of the Knowing Eye clan pursue old books: access to the libraries of Jincheng, investigations in the Oni hills, and surveys of the northern mountains are all practical steps in the dragon-search chain. This is not simply a matter of accumulating enough points to summon a dragon; the player must open diplomatic, logistical, and geographic routes before the legend becomes actionable evidence.【Local narrative text】【Local scripts】

At the same time, Balrijin must learn to cooperate with human states. The missions permit the recruitment of human auxiliaries, strengthen political and financial ties with the Blue Scarf movement, and envision the hill neighbors becoming companions in a shared faith. Balris worship does not automatically make every neighboring state a friend: diplomats, allied trust, and border security remain scarce resources. The early missions' friendly posture and their later hostility toward the Command can coexist, but not every Halessi war should be rewritten as history that had already happened in 1444.【Local scripts】【Local narrative text】

After Balris Returns

The turning point of the dragon search is not “find a powerful ruler and finish.” The current mission text presents Balris as lonely and sorrowful, an entity that must be persuaded to stay; the player must make the country's society, alliances, and palace worthy of his expectations. If this phase succeeds, the dragon in turn challenges the power held by the old sage class. The missions propose weakening clerical privileges, establishing a constitution, and moving toward a council republic, so Balrijin's political growth is not simply the expansion of a theocracy.【Local narrative text】【Local scripts】

The Goldscale Bank is an equally important line. Gold wealth can produce inflation, while the Grasping Tail clan seeks to establish a national financial institution and then connect Goldscale currency to the Blue Scarf banking system. The ending text depicts the two sides as close enough that some want unification while others argue for retaining two states and deepening cooperation; this is a debatable political proposal, not confirmation that every campaign automatically annexes the Blue Scarf republic. The late game also contains a design for protecting and subordinating ruin kingdoms, showing that this is not an entirely non-expansionist, gentle route.【Local narrative text】【Local scripts】

Balrijin's real problem is therefore how to honor three promises at once: its Goldscale traditions, the human neighbors willing to ally with it, and the new political standards set by Balris. If the player focuses only on the dragon search and neglects finances and military power, a weak country may not survive to the later chapters; if the player focuses only on conquest, the most distinctive clan and republic transformation will be missed. The Wiki's Sage Council already permits clan favoritism, so the later constitutional reform in the missions is not an arbitrary narrative rupture.【Offline Wiki】【Local narrative text】

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 66/100｜Authoritarianism 45/100｜Magic↔Artifice 69/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 77/100)｜Pluralism 76/100. Stage shift: Sage Council and dragon search (Authoritarianism 68) → Balris' reforms and council (Authoritarianism 25).

The v2.1 value is Good (74/100), with an improving trajectory. Human auxiliaries, cross-cultural diplomacy, banking stability, and constitutional reform express public benefit and recognition across peoples; sage privileges, hostility toward the Command, and dependent policies for ruin kingdoms reduce restraint. War and expansion themselves are not counted against the score. Cross-cultural auxiliaries, alliances with neighbors, financial stabilization, and power reform have clear public benefits; the hostile narrative toward the Command, policies that make ruin kingdoms dependent, and sage privileges limit the evaluation. War and great-power ambitions themselves are not included in the good/evil judgment. Players who enjoy a small-country search for a deity intertwined with political reform, and who are willing to manage diplomacy and finance, are a good fit; players who want uninterrupted early conquest and do not want the dragon-search missions constrained by regional requirements may find the pace slow.【Local scripts】【Local narrative text】

Reddit players especially praise the dragon-search story and repeatedly complain that, in older versions, the Command and the Yixia situation could interrupt the clues; recent discussions also touch on changes to religion, succession, and government reform. These only show what players encountered in different versions; they cannot replace the current scripts as evidence of whether a mission is reachable.【Community view】

The current offline-Wiki background, player posts, and specific local line references are listed in the original research evidence. The bounded English-text review and source receipt are listed separately in the translation receipt.

National Ideas (Source Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. The traditions take effect when this idea set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as the idea group is filled; the ambition takes effect after all seven ideas are unlocked. Only the national ideas themselves are listed; racial, government, and mission rewards are not mixed into these numbers. A formed country's new ideas do not automatically stack with the old set. Idea descriptions may recall history or describe a future ideal and do not automatically mean that the events already happened in 1444.

Balrijin (Y85) — Balrijin Ideas

Tradition: Balrijin Traditions

Effects: Construction cost: -10%; Improve relations: +25%.

Idea 1: Bringers of Good Fortune

Since time immemorial, the people of Yanshen have treasured golden kobold scales as glittering good-luck charms. Many a foreign dignitary has summited the mountains of Balrisen to acquire them, bearing extravagant gifts to exchange in return. It was only a matter of time before the kobolds themselves began to adorn the highest courts in the land. As living portents of good fortune, Goldscale kobolds are honored guests of Yanshen's elite.

Effect: Diplomatic reputation: +200% (inherited display; the script value is diplomatic_reputation = 2; unit conversion unverified).

Idea 2: Memories of the Great Burning

When Jaher first came to these lands, with hair and spears of gold, we thought him indeed 'Chosen' -- by almighty Balris. Unfortunately, we would learn the truth of the matter in the most awful of ways. After his son Elizar failed in the campaign against Thidinkai, Jaher ordered him confined to camp, and limited to strategic duties. Unfortunately for us, once there, Elizar encountered rumors that 'the hills were filled with gold', and gathered a small expeditionary force to loot said riches and deliver them as restitution to his father.

Of course, these rumors mostly referred to us. We attempted to correct their misunderstanding, but Elizar was not interested in dialogue. His force seized what little riches we had, and smashed the monasteries looking for more. In Elizar's fury and disappointment, he set many ablaze, a monstrous act our people remember as 'The Great Burning'.

Elizar was soon punished, sent back to Bulwar for his sins. But we also remember what happened next: when Jaher was assassinated, the Goldscale kobolds rose up to cast off the elven yoke, and the mountain springs ran red with their blood. Just as it was then, our righteous fervor in defense of Balrijin still burns brighter than any sun.

Effect: Army morale: +10%.

Idea 3: Balris' Devoted

Balris the Gold. Bringer of Songs, Slayer of Ignorance, Wisest of Masters. The sagas record that his coming was heralded by a great and thunderous roar, cracking the groundsky and forcing our people to the surface for the first time. By his almighty power, he could have devoured us, enslaved us, or simply driven us away; but he did not. Instead, the Paragon of Benevolence lived alongside our ancestors in the mountain caves, and opened our eyes to a whole new world. Before his countless lessons, our people sung only songs of sorrow and mourning, and built only what we needed to survive. Now, we sing his praises to the golden light of the sunrise, and carve resplendent cliffside temples in his name. And though he only remained with us for a short time, we will never forget his eternal promise: To return one day, and walk alongside us once more. United in his exaltation, under the flag of the Golden Dragon, we named our nation after the object of all our hopes, and our one true god: Balrijin.

Effects: Tolerance of the true faith: +1; Devotion: +0.5; Legitimacy: +0.5; Republican tradition: +0.15; Horde unity: +0.5.

Idea 4: Dragon Dances

Among the wise Clan Sages of the Golden Council of Balrijin, the Master Sage is chosen to act as the final decider in all disputes. But, in emulation of our patient and benevolent Teacher, Master Sages often decide to remain impartial. There can be only one way resolve such an impasse: a martial arts duel. Known as a 'Dragon Dance', this holy tradition demands we tirelessly hone our skills and train our bodies into brilliant golden weapons, all for the sake of Balrijin's blessed peace. And when we turn those weapons against foreign invaders, they will be all the sharper.

Effect: Army tradition decay: -0.01.

Idea 5: A Kobold in Every City

From the noble courts, Goldscale kobolds proliferated into Yanshen's great cities. Over time, this diaspora evolved into a network of contacts and merchants involved in the lucrative scale trade. In markets and plazas across the land, one can always find a glimmer of gold shining among the crowd, spreading the jewelcrafts and other wares of Balrijin far and wide.

Effect: Global trade power: +10%.

Idea 6: Works of Golden Scales

'Let's face it, we just can't compete! Try and sell a cloak, they sell a cloak with gold trim! Invent a new gizmo, they'll make the same thing but shinier! How are we supposed to outproduce these lizards when they've got gold falling off their bodies?!' - A very frustrated gnome learning why Goldscales dominate the Yanshen luxury market

Effect: Production efficiency: +15%.

Idea 7: The Goldscale Hoard

When we first established contact with our western kobold brethren, we were shocked - by their gaudy colors, their crude culture, and the very fact of their existence. It seemed they, too recounted tales of great dragons, but all these wicked 'chromatics' had taught them was to hoard their wealth in giant underground piles. Yet the Wisest of Masters teaches us that true justice lies not in banishing the wicked, but in transfiguring evil to righteousness. We will adopt the western tradition of hoards, but rather than piling up coins and baubles, we will require every kobold who comes of age to submit one of their scales, with a piece of wisdom written on the back. After all, our people are our real treasures - and wisdom is true wealth.

Effect: Technology cost: -5%.

Ambition: Balrijin Ambition

Effect: Development cost: -10%.
